sentences.text: The top line of the outline is a theorem of Main.lean.

It states that the value DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s of the Mathlib library is not zero for every DirichletCharacter χ of that library and every complex number s with real part above 1/2, except when χ is the trivial character and s is 1.
The 37 lines below it state the largest steps that the proof passes through, which are the ones that gather at least 10,000 declarations in the graph of the README.
This document says for each of the 38 lines what its Lean statement claims, in plain sentences and in ordinary notation.
The readings were written by a language model and checked by further runs of the same model.
No mathematician has checked them.
Each reading has a separate paragraph for what a name only suggests, and the check looked for meanings asserted outside that paragraph.
The model run that wrote a reading also rated its confidence.
High means that it saw the statement and what every project definition in it says.
Medium means that it saw the form of the claim with some names left unopened.
Low means that it saw little more than a chain of named conditions.
One line is rated high, 24 are rated medium and 13 are rated low.
README.md defines the outline, its lines, the head and the wrappers of a line and the verb gathers.
The readings are of the source after the merge of upstream main on 2026-11-22.

sections.title: What the top of the outline says

sentences.text: The numbers are the line numbers of the outline, and every name in code font is a name of the source.
A reading covers the statement of the head of a line.
It covers neither the proof nor the statements of the wrappers.
The sentences below about a proof, about the wrapper of line 1 and about the names of Row come from the source files, which the model session that wrote this document read directly.
A premise of a line is a hypothesis that its theorem takes before its named conclusion.
A condition inside the conclusion is not counted as a premise.
Line 1 has no premises.
Its head everyCharacter states the proposition that the code calls EveryCharacter.
For every N ≥ 1, every DirichletCharacter χ of level N and every complex number s with real part above 1/2, the value LFunction χ s is not zero, unless χ is the trivial character and s is 1.
The wrapper of the line is the theorem of Main.lean, and its proposition DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf in Statements.lean has word for word the same definition.
Line 2 hangs from line 1 and derives EveryCharacter from one premise.
The statement of line 2 writes that premise as Row0b applied to the condition IsRecT.
The code names the same proposition Row, and line 33 writes it as Row0b recT, where recT is the code's name for that condition.
The definitions show the form of Row.

For every CM number field E, every prime l, every a ≥ 1, every π of the code's type CuspSub that meets IsRegAlg and every χ of the type HChar for which the pair meets PolarizedPair, there exist a homomorphism r into the invertible a by a matrices over the field that the code calls Qbar l, an integer and a function HT that meet a condition PropsB.
The statement also quantifies over an algebraic closure of E and an isomorphism from Qbar l to ℂ, which this summary leaves out.
The names suggest Galois representations attached to automorphic representations, which the Lean text that the reading was made from does not show.
Line 33 hangs from line 1 and states Row0b recT with no premises.
The proof of the head of line 1 in MainConclusion.lean applies the theorem of line 2 to the theorem of line 33.
Lines 3 and 30 hang from line 2.
Line 3 derives EveryCharacter from a bundle of three fields and a proposition VWin.
Two fields of the bundle are Row.
The other field is RecTExists, which says that for every number field and every prime of it a map exists that meets a condition IsRecT.
VWin says that a condition VWinAt ψ 401 holds for every primitive Dirichlet character ψ.
Line 30 derives VWin from three named statements.
Line 31 hangs from line 30 and line 32 from line 31, and each derives VWin from one bundle of named statements.
Lines 4 and 24 hang from line 3.
Line 4 derives EveryCharacter from seven premises.
Two premises are bundles.
The text that was read shows 28 named statements of the first and 29 of the second before it is cut.
Three premises are the propositions ThetaIntegralsAgree, LocalMatching and CovolumeBoundOfX.
The last two are RecTExists and VWin.
Line 24 derives CovolumeBoundOfX from fifteen named propositions.
Lines 5 and 23 hang from line 4.
Line 5 concludes that a record of the type HypsAlt S0.NL DefiniteSideCondition exists.
Its premises are six of the seven premises of line 4 and one more.
Line 23 concludes the proposition ZeroFreeAll, which says that every primitive Dirichlet character ψ meets the condition ψ.ZeroFreeAbove (1/2).
Its premises are the existence of such a record, VWin and a statement Green.
Lines 6 to 22 hang below line 5.
Their statements are written in a vocabulary of the project, with names such as FamP, LinkedAt, Closed and HypsAlt, which the definitions shown to the readers do not open.
The readers saw definitions up to three steps away from the statement, as the next section describes.
A person can follow which named condition follows from which, and the mathematics behind the names stays closed.
Lines 1, 33, 35 and 37 have no premises.
Each of the other 34 lines derives one or more named statements from named statements.
By the README, a line hangs below another when the five theorems depend on the lower line only by way of the upper one.
A line without premises can therefore still have lines hanging below it.
A lower line can also have premises that the line above it lacks, as line 3 has RecTExists and VWin.
The proof of the upper line then has to supply them, and the readings do not show how, since they cover statements only.
dossier.py wrote a dossier for the head of each line.
A dossier holds the Lean statement, the statements of the wrappers of the line, and definitions at three levels.
Level one holds the definitions that the statement names, level two those that the definitions of level one name, and level three those that the definitions of level two name.
A dossier stops after three levels or after 45 definitions, whichever comes first.
Definitions of the first two levels are shown with their bodies and those of the third level without.
The 38 dossiers hold 1,622 definitions and about one million characters.
A first reader wrote, from the dossier alone, what the theorem states, its premises in order, its conclusion, the statement in ordinary notation, the definitions it relied on, and its confidence.
It wrote in a separate field what the names suggest beyond the text.
A second reader wrote its own reading from the same dossier without seeing the first.
A check compared both readings with the Lean text.
It looked for a missing or an added premise, a wrong quantifier, a wrong number or exponent, a wrong conclusion, and a meaning asserted for a name whose body the dossier does not show.
A first reading with an error was corrected and checked again.
The first reader, the second reader, the check and the corrections are runs of the command line tool Claude Code.
Each run was started in a folder that held only the dossiers and, for the check, the two readings.
The briefs of the four roles are in briefs/.
The reading printed for a line is the first reading after correction.
The second readings served for the comparison and were left as they were.
The check found 16 errors in the first readings of ten lines and four errors in the second readings of three lines.
Each error was in the detail inside a premise or a conclusion.
A reading called a type a group although the dossier does not show that it is one, left out a condition inside a premise, or gave a wrong count.
No error changed the list of premises of a line or the name of its conclusion.
After correction all 38 printed readings passed the check.
Eight of the ten passed after one round, line 7 after two and line 10 after three.
The last corrections of lines 7 and 10 are the exception to the separate runs.
The model session that wrote this document made them directly and removed the detail that the check had faulted, and the check then passed both.
A model of another maker then repeated the check.
Gemini, run in the Antigravity editor, read the same dossiers and the printed readings with the brief of the check and faulted 20 of the 38 readings with 71 findings.
Each finding was compared with the words of the reading and with the Lean text of the dossier by further runs of Claude Code.
No finding showed a reading that states what the Lean text contradicts.

In 21 cases the summary of a premise left out a quantifier, an argument or a hypothesis without saying so, and in 16 cases the wording was inexact, with an unbound variable, a dropped argument or a claim stronger than the dossier shows.

In 17 cases the reading uses an ordinary word for an object whose body the dossier does not show, and 23 findings did not hold, most of them because another field of the same reading gives the detail said to be missing.
The 16 lines with cases of the first two kinds were changed in 40 places, and an entry says so when it was changed.
A summary of a premise now names what it leaves out.
The 16 changed readings were then checked once more by runs of Claude Code, each in a folder with one dossier and one reading.
Twelve passed.
In the other four the check found five errors, four of them ordinary words for names without a shown body and one a premise of the wrapper theorems of line 8 that the changed text had left out.
The five were corrected with the text of the check, and a second check of those four readings found no error.
The other cases of ordinary words stand as they were.

An entry below shows, in this order, where the head lies, what the theorem states, its premises and its conclusion, a display of the statement in ordinary notation, the names that the reading does not open, what the names suggest, the confidence with its reason, and what the check found.
A reading can say that definitions were left out, which refers to the limit of 45 definitions of its dossier.

sections.title: A deeper reading of lines 6 to 22

sentences.text: The first readings of lines 6 to 22 stayed at the level of names.

After the record D7 was opened in D7.md, each of these 17 lines was read once more by a run that saw the dossier of the line, the whole Lean text of D7 with the 282 definitions below it, and the ten readings of GLOSSARY.md.
The briefs are briefs/reread-reader.txt and briefs/reread-check.txt.
The 17 deeper readings open 107 names that the first readings left unopened, and the number of names they leave unopened falls from 180 to 124.
They also say more, and the check found more to fault.
It found 43 errors in 16 of the 17 readings.
After those were corrected with the text that the check supplied, a second check found 46 further errors in 15 readings, and they were corrected in the same way.
Most errors of the second round are of one kind.
The reading uses a word of mathematics, such as irreducible or unitary, for a name whose body no file shows.
Gemini then checked the deeper readings as it checked the printed ones.
It found line 13 faithful and made 106 findings on the other 16 readings.
Runs of Claude Code compared each finding with the Lean text.
Three findings did not hold and 103 did.
None of the 103 is a sentence that the Lean text contradicts.
In 50 the reading uses a word of mathematics for a name whose body no file shows, in 31 the wording is inexact, and in 22 a quantifier, an argument or a hypothesis is left out without a note.

The weightiest are in line 8, where the reading stated two bounds without the hypotheses under which the Lean text places them, and in line 18, where it named a density theorem for a statement of existence.
All 103 passages were replaced with text that the run checked against the Lean text.
The 16 changed deeper readings were then checked again, each by a run of Claude Code in a folder with its dossier, the text of D7, the glossary and the reading.
Fourteen passed.
In lines 12 and 22 the check found one error each, a word of mathematics for a name whose body no file shows, and both were corrected with the text of the check.
A further check of the two corrected readings found no error.
As a test of the check itself, two numbers of the deeper reading of line 8 were changed to wrong ones in a copy, and the check found both.
The check and the readings come from one maker's models, and Gemini has not read the corrected texts.

The head is UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter, in the module Development › Automorphic Arithmetic › Character Boxes › Main Conclusion.
The line gathers 760,227 declarations and is the top of the outline.
Folded into the line is the wrapper LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re.
The theorem asserts, with no premises, the proposition that the code calls EveryCharacter.

Unfolded, it says that for every nonzero natural number N, every Dirichlet character χ of level N with complex values and every complex number s with real part greater than 1/2, if χ is not the trivial character or s is not 1, then the library value DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s is not zero.

A wrapper theorem in the module Main, named LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re, is folded into this line and asserts a proposition called DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf whose body the dossier does not show.
Conclusion.
For all N ≠ 0, all χ of level N and all complex s with Re(s) > 1/2 and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1), the value LFunction χ s is nonzero.
The reading does not open the names DirichletCharacter ℂ N, DirichletCharacter.LFunction and DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf.
The next sentences are a suggestion from the names, which the Lean text of the dossier does not show.

The names suggest that LFunction is the analytically continued Dirichlet L-function, in which case the statement says no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above 1/2, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis that includes the Riemann zeta function at N = 1, and the wrapper name suggests it restates the same claim.
The reader's confidence is high.
The statement of the head and the one definition it names are shown in full, and the names of the standard library remain unfolded.
The proposition DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf of the wrapper also remains unfolded in the dossier.

The line gathers 577,248 declarations and hangs from line 1, everyCharacter.
The theorem says that if the proposition Row0b holds for the notion Rc that sends a pair (h, rc) to the condition IsRecT h rc, then EveryCharacter holds.

The premise Row0b says that for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, every natural number a ≥ 1, every π of type CuspSub E a and every χ of type HChar over the maximal real subfield of E, if the class of π satisfies a condition that the code calls IsRegAlg and the pair (π, χ) satisfies PolarizedPair, then there exist a group homomorphism r from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL_a(Qbar l), an integer wt and a function HT from the ring embeddings of E into Qbar l to multisets of integers such that PropsB Rc π ι r wt HT holds.
The conclusion is the nonvanishing statement of line 1.
Premise 1.
Row0b holds with the notion Rc taken to be the map (h, rc) ↦ IsRecT h rc.
Conclusion.
EveryCharacter holds, that is, LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for all N ≠ 0, all χ of level N and all complex s with Re(s) > 1/2 and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1).
The reading does not open the names LawsT, PropsB, CuspSub E a, PolarizedPair, HChar and IsRegAlg.
The next sentences are a suggestion from the names, which the Lean text of the dossier does not show.

The names suggest that the premise is the existence of l-adic Galois representations attached to regular algebraic polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_a over CM fields, with local-global compatibility measured against a local Langlands reciprocity map, and that the conclusion is the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions.
The reader's confidence is medium.

The outer shape of the premise and the whole conclusion are visible, but the conditions inside PropsB, CuspSub and PolarizedPair, and LawsT, a name inside the body of IsRecT, rest on names without bodies and eight definitions were left out.
